questions.text: Do you work, or are you a student?
questions.say: Good afternoon. My name is Daniel, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Do you work, or are you a student?

questions.text: How do you travel to your workplace or your place of study?
questions.say: How do you travel to your workplace or your place of study?

questions.text: What is a normal working or study day like for you?
questions.say: What is a normal working or study day like for you?

questions.text: Would you like to work or study in another country?
questions.say: Would you like to work or study in another country?
Now let's move on to talk about cleaning. Do you like cleaning?

questions.text: Who does most of the cleaning in your home?
questions.say: Who does most of the cleaning in your home?

questions.text: Did you have to help with the cleaning when you were a child?

Now let's move on to talk about podcasts. Do you listen to podcasts?

questions.text: Do you prefer podcasts or the radio?
questions.say: Do you prefer podcasts or the radio?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you taught someone something.
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt about teaching this person.

questions.text: Describe a time when you taught someone something.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you taught someone something. You should say: who you taught; what you taught them; how you taught it; and explain how you felt about teaching this person.

questions.text: Do you enjoy explaining things to other people?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you enjoy explaining things to other people?

questions.text: What makes someone good at explaining things?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you taught someone something, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all teaching. What makes someone good at explaining things?

questions.text: Is teaching a respected job in your country?
questions.say: Is teaching a respected job in your country?

questions.text: Do you think it is harder to teach adults or children?
questions.say: Do you think it is harder to teach adults or children?

questions.text: Do people learn better by doing things or by reading about them?
questions.say: Now let's talk about ways of learning. Do people learn better by doing things or by reading about them?

questions.text: What are the advantages of learning from friends rather than from a teacher?
questions.say: What are the advantages of learning from friends rather than from a teacher?

questions.text: How will the way people learn change in the future?
questions.say: How will the way people learn change in the future?
